newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel okays settler Hebron groundwork -settlers.
newsitem.headline: Israel okays settler Hebron groundwork -settlers.

text.p: Jewish settlers in the volatile West Bank town of Hebron said on Friday they had received a permit to do groundwork for six new homes in one of their existing enclaves.

"What happened is he gave a permit to do groundwork," Hebron settler spokesman Noam Arnon told Reuters when asked about a Maariv daily report that Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai had approved the building of new homes.
Arnon said there was as yet no permit to begin the actual construction on the planned six new homes in the Avraham Avinu Jewish enclave.
The Defence Ministry, in charge of permitting construction in the West Bank and Gaza Strip which Israel occupied in 1967, refused to comment.
"There is anti-Semitic discrimination against the Jews here that the Arabs build thousands of homes and Jews have to wait months to get permits," Arnon told Reuters.

"We demand the free right for Jews to buy homes in all parts of Hebron and to build without hindrance and if they don't allow us to build freely, we'll weigh turning to the international court in Hague."
Arnon said he did not know when the groundwork would begin because contractors had yet to be lined up.
In January, Israel's present right-wing government, under a commitment made by the previous dovish government, handed over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule.

Clashes have periodically erupted between Israeli troops and Palestinians in Hebron along the line now dividing the sides since Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

The posting by an Israeli woman of a picture depicting Islam's Prophet Mohammad as a pig in the town in June further angered its 100,000 Palestinian residents. Some 400 Jews live in several heavily fortified enclaves in the Hebron.
